model_name: hierarchical crowding with hydrodynamic hindrance and reversible binding

derivation: Kozeny-Carman-like permeability with particle hydrodynamic hindrance
provenance.hypothesis: local crowding and binding-state residence times differ from a mean-matched scalar diffusivity

equations.permeability: K_nano = a^2 chi_n^3 / (2 phi_n^2 + chi_n phi_n (1 + interaction_strength phi_n))
equations.binding: free -> bound: k_on(x) = k_on0 (1 + interaction_strength phi_n(x)) chi_n(x); bound -> free: k_off(x) = k_off0
equations.diffusion_equation: partial_t p = partial_x (D(x) partial_x p) - k_on p_free + k_off p_bound
equations.adjusted_comparator: D_adj = spatial mean of D(x) on transient cells

limitations: One-dimensional bounded domain and a deterministic sinusoidal obstacle field are not a measured cell geometry.
The Kozeny-Carman-like closure and binding rates are mechanistic assumptions, not fitted internal data.
A finite-volume absorbing outlet estimates first exit, not a biological target-search time.
The scalar comparator is mean-matched and therefore tests spatial/binding mechanisms, not a claim that scalar diffusion is generally sufficient.
